translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Joel son of Bethuel.
Hear this, elders, and listen, all inhabitants of the land. Has anything like this happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?
Tell this to your children, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.
What the caterpillar left, the locust ate; what the locust left, the locust grub ate; and what the locust grub left, the mildew consumed.
Sober up from your wine, you drunkards, and weep. Come to your senses, all you who drink wine to become drunk, because joy and gladness have been taken away from your mouths.
For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and innumerable. Its teeth are a lion’s teeth, and its fangs are those of a young lion.
It has ruined my vine and shattered my fig tree. It stripped it completely bare and threw it away, and made its branches white.
Lament to me like a bride dressed in sackcloth mourning her husband.
Offerings and sacrifices have been removed from the house of the Lord. Mourn, priests who serve at the altar.
For the fields have been devastated. Let the land mourn, because the wheat has been ruined, the wine has dried up, and the oil has dwindled.
Lament, farmers, over your crops, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest has perished from the fields.
The vine has dried up; the fig, the pomegranate, the palm, and the apple have dwindled, and every tree in the fields has withered, because the children of men have put joy to shame.

Dress in sackcloth and beat your breasts, priests. Mourn, you who serve at the altar. Go in and sleep in sackcloth, servants of God, because offerings and sacrifices have ceased in the house of your God.
Consecrate a fast; proclaim a time of supplication. Gather the elders and all the inhabitants of your land into the house of your God, and cry out to the Lord with all your heart.
Woe to me! Woe to me! Woe to me on that day! For the day of the Lord is near; it will come like devastation from devastation.
Food has run out before your eyes, and joy and gladness have ceased from the house of your God.
The heifers leaped in their stalls. The storehouses have been ruined; the granaries have collapsed, because the wheat has been scorched by the hot wind.
What shall I store in them? The herds of cattle wept because they had no pasture, and the flocks of sheep perished.
To you, Lord, I will cry out, because fire has destroyed the beauty of the wilderness, and flame has consumed every tree in the fields.
The wild beast too looked to you, because the streams of water have dried up, and fire has consumed the beauty of the wilderness.
Blow the trumpet in Zion; make a proclamation on my holy mountain. Let all the inhabitants of the land gather, because the day of the Lord has arrived, because it is near.

A day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and mist. Like dawn, a great and mighty army will spread over the mountains. Its like has never existed from ancient times, nor will its like arise again afterward, from generation to generation.
Before it is a consuming fire, and behind it a blazing flame. The land before it is like a garden of delight, and behind it a devastated plain. Nothing will escape it.
Its appearance is like the appearance of horses, and they will charge like mounted riders.
With a sound like the rattling of chariots, they will raid across the mountain peaks, like the sound of a fiery flame consuming reeds, like a great and mighty army prepared for battle.
Before them nations will be crushed, and every face will be like a scorched pot.
They will charge like champions and climb the walls like warriors. Each will go his own way, and they must not turn aside from their paths.
Let no man separate from his brother or his companion. Laden with their weapons, they will advance; they will fall under arrows but will not perish.
They will reach the city and run along the walls. They will climb into houses and enter through windows like thieves.
Before them the earth will be troubled and the heavens will shake. The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will hide their light.
And the Lord will raise his voice before his army, for his camp is very large, and mighty is his work of war. For the day of the Lord is great, great and very glorious, and who can withstand it?
And now the Lord your God says, “Return to me with all your heart, with fasting, weeping, and mourning.”
Tear your hearts, not your clothes, and return to the Lord your God, for he is merciful and compassionate, patient and abundant in mercy, and he relents from bringing harm.
Who knows whether he will turn and relent and leave a blessing behind him, with offerings and sacrifices for the Lord our God?
Sound the trumpet in Zion, consecrate a fast, proclaim supplications.
Gather the people, consecrate the assembly, choose the elders, gather the nursing children. Let the bridegroom leave his room and the bride her bridal chamber.

Between the steps and the altar, let the priests and the Lord’s ministers weep and say, “Spare your people, Lord, and do not give your inheritance over to disgrace, for nations to rule over it, lest they say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”
Then the Lord was jealous for his land and spared his people.
And the Lord answered his people and said, “Look, I am sending you grain, wine, and oil, and you will be filled with them. I will no longer make you an object of reproach among the nations.”

I will drive the northerner away from you and banish him to a waterless land. I will destroy his front in the eastern sea and his rear in the western sea. His putrid discharge will rise, and his stench will spread, because his deeds have become great.
Take courage, land; rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has done great things for you.
Take courage, wild animals, for the pastures of the wilderness have grown green. The tree has yielded its fruit; the vine and the fig tree have yielded their bounty.
Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, for the Lord has given you food for righteousness. He will send you rain, early and late, as before.
The threshing floors will be full of wheat, and the presses will overflow with wine and oil.
I will repay you for the years whose harvest the locust, the young locust, and the caterpillar ate—my great army, which I sent against you.
You will eat abundantly and be satisfied, and you will bless the name of the Lord your God, who has done wonderful things for you. My people will never again be put to shame.
And you will know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no one besides me. And my people will never be put to shame.
After this, I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy, your elders will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
Even on my male servants and my female servants I will pour out my Spirit in those days, and they will prophesy.
I will give signs in heaven above and on earth below: blood, fire, and a swirling cloud of smoke.
The sun will turn to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and glorious day of the Lord comes.

Everyone who calls on the name of the Lord will be saved. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be survivors, as the Lord has said, and those who receive the good news, whom the Lord will call to himself.
For behold, in those days and at that time, when I restore the captives of Judea and Jerusalem,

And I will gather all the nations and bring them down into the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will judge them on account of my people and my inheritance, Israel, whom they scattered among all the nations, and because they divided up my land.
They cast lots for my people, gave boys as payment to prostitutes, and sold girls for wine, which they drank.

And you too, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of the Philistines—are you still against me? Are you repaying me for something, or will you hold a grudge against me? Swiftly and urgently I will bring your repayment back upon your own heads.
Because you took my silver and gold and carried the very finest and beautiful vessels into your temples,
and sold the sons of Judah and the sons of Jerusalem to the Greeks, to drive them far from their own borders.
Now I will raise them up from the place to which you sold them, and I will bring your repayment back upon your own heads.
I will deliver your sons and daughters into the hands of the sons of Judah, and they will sell them into captivity to a distant nation far away, for the Lord has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: appoint a time for battle; awaken the warriors. Gather together and go up, all you men of war.
Beat your plowshares into swords and your sickles into spears. Let the weak take courage and say, “I am strong.”
Gather and come, all you surrounding nations; assemble there. Let the peaceful become warriors.
Let all the nations awaken and go up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the surrounding nations.
Put in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come in and tread, for the winepress is full and the vats overflow, because their wicked deeds have multiplied.
Voices resounded in the Valley of Judgment, for the day of the Lord is near in the Valley of Judgment.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the stars will hide their light.
And the Lord will roar from Zion and raise his voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth will shake.
But the Lord will spare his people and strengthen the sons of Israel.
And you will know that I am the Lord God, who dwells in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will no longer pass through it.

And on that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, the hills will flow with milk, and all the springs of Judah will pour out water. A spring will come out of the house of the Lord and water the Valley of Lots.
Egypt will become a ruin, and Edom a desolate plain, because of the wrongs done to the sons of Judah, because they shed innocent blood in their land.
But Judea will remain inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
And I will demand an accounting for their blood and will not acquit the guilty. And the Lord will dwell in Zion.
